# Mathematical audit

Verdict: pass as a conditional representation-transfer theorem; fail as an
unconditional Yang--Mills result.

| Gate | Verdict | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| objects and domains typed | pass | packages, arrows, observable cores, and index families have declared roles |
| category language controlled | pass | full categorical structure is claimed only for exact total arrows; “morphism” is otherwise local vocabulary |
| error composition | pass | triangle inequality plus pullback seminorm; associativity shown algebraically |
| recovery distinct from exactness | pass | forgotten and recovered entries are separate; supplement rejects invalid profiles |
| positivity used explicitly | pass | spectral measure is positive; no cancellation argument is hidden |
| dense centered core | essential and stated | excludes vacuum and prevents a hidden low-energy sector |
| fixed-\(t\) convergence | pass | sufficient because the exponential bound holds for every \(t\ge0\) and the limit is taken separately at each \(t\) |
| index-independent rate | essential and stated | collapsing-gap countermodel shows pointwise positive rates are insufficient |
| target conclusion | pass | vanishing of spectral measures on \([0,m)\) over a dense vacuum complement excludes spectrum in \((0,m)\) |
| unique vacuum | stated | needed to identify the centered complement with all nonvacuum states |
| OS corollary | conditional | reconstruction, positivity, continuum existence, and core density are premises, not outputs |
| finite verifier scope | pass | code certifies exact finite examples and profile arithmetic only |

The central positive-Laplace lemma is standard spectral calculus. The paper's
mathematical contribution is its placement in a typed recovery theorem and the
minimal countermodel suite, not a claim to invent spectral-measure positivity.

No proof assumes the desired target gap. The shared rate enters as a Euclidean
bound on recovered quadratic forms; the theorem derives spectral exclusion
only after convergence and density are supplied independently.
